text: Assumption 1 . (i) The set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}$ is nonempty, closed, and convex. The set $Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p}$ is nonempty, compact, and convex, with $D_{Y}:=\max_{y\in Y}\lVert y\rVert>0.$ (ii) For almost every $\omega$ , the sample loss $f(\cdot,\cdot;\omega)$ is differentiable on a neighborhood of $X\times Y$ . (iii) The function $F$ is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of $X\times Y$ , and there exists $L>0$ such that, for all $(x,y),(x^{\prime},y^{\prime})\in X\times Y$ , $\lVert\nabla F(x^{\prime},y^{\prime})-\nabla F(x,y)\rVert\leq L\lVert(x^{\prime}-x,y^{\prime}-y)\rVert.$ (2) (iv) For every $x\in X$ , the function $F(x,\cdot)$ is concave on $Y$ . The primal value function satisfies $\phi(x):=\max_{y\in Y}F(x,y),\qquad x\in X,\qquad\phi_{\inf}:=\inf_{x\in X}\phi(x)>-\infty.$ (3)

Theorem 1 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Then Algorithm 1 , with the parameter choices in ( 33 ) and ( 79 ), satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{V}_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}]\leq\mathcal{V}_{t}-\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{D}_{t}^{0}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t}]-\frac{\beta}{8L}\lVert\nabla p(z_{t})\rVert^{2}+\frac{300\sigma^{2}}{Lm}.$ (89)

Assumption 3 . There exists $\mu>0$ such that, for every $x\in X$ and $y,y^{\prime}\in Y$ , $F(x,y^{\prime})\leq F(x,y)+\langle\nabla_{y}F(x,y),y^{\prime}-y\rangle-\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert y^{\prime}-y\rVert^{2}.$ (98) Define the condition number $\kappa:=L/\mu$ . The joint $L$ -smoothness in Assumption 1 implies $0<\mu\leq L$ and hence $\kappa\geq 1$ .

Theorem 2 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 , 2 , and 3 hold. Fix a known bound $\overline{B}\geq B$ and set $T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{128L\overline{B}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad m=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{38400\sigma^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\}.$ (102) Then SPDE returns a point satisfying ( 7 ), and $\displaystyle N_{\rm sc}$ $\displaystyle\leq 3\left(1+\frac{128L\overline{B}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right)\left(1+\frac{38400\sigma^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right)$ $\displaystyle=O\!\left(1+\frac{(L\overline{B}+\sigma^{2})\sqrt{\kappa}}{\varepsilon^{2}}+\frac{L\overline{B}\sigma^{2}\kappa}{\varepsilon^{4}}\right).$ (103) For fixed $L,\overline{B}$ and $\sigma>0$ , this gives $T=O(\sqrt{\kappa}\varepsilon^{-2}),\qquad m=O(\sqrt{\kappa}\varepsilon^{-2}),\qquad N_{\rm sc}=O(\kappa\varepsilon^{-4}).$ (104) If $\sigma=0$ , then $m=1$ and $N_{\rm sc}=O(\sqrt{\kappa}\varepsilon^{-2})$ .

Theorem 3 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Choose a known upper bound independent of $\varepsilon,\tau$ satisfying $\overline{B}\geq B$ , where $B$ is defined in ( 29 ). Given $\varepsilon>0$ , set $\tau=\min\left\{L,\frac{\varepsilon}{2D_{Y}}\right\},$ (105) choose $h,\alpha,k$ by ( 33 ) and $\beta$ by ( 79 ), and set $T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{256L\overline{B}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad m=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{76800\sigma^{2}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\}.$ (106) Then the output of Algorithm 1 satisfies ( 7 ). The number $N$ of stochastic full-gradient oracle calls satisfies the explicit bound $N\leq 3mT\leq 3\left(1+\frac{256L\overline{B}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right)\left(1+\frac{76800\sigma^{2}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right).$ (107) Let $K_{\varepsilon}:=\max\left\{1,\sqrt{\frac{2LD_{Y}}{\varepsilon}}\right\}.$ (108) Then $N=O\!\left(1+\frac{(L\overline{B}+\sigma^{2})K_{\varepsilon}}{\varepsilon^{2}}+\frac{L\overline{B}\sigma^{2}K_{\varepsilon}^{2}}{\varepsilon^{4}}\right).$ (109) For a fixed problem, initialization, $\overline{B}$ , and $\sigma>0$ , as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ , the iteration count is $T=O(\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ and the batch size is $m=O(\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ , so $N=O(\varepsilon^{-5})$ .

Remark 1 . The theorem provides an upper bound for a general unbiased oracle with bounded variance, using a fixed batch size while retaining the single-loop structure. The $O(\varepsilon^{-5})$ bound counts individual sample-gradient calls; the iteration count is $O(\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ . The guarantee concerns the expected squared game-stationarity residual of the original problem.

Assumption 4 . In addition to Assumption 2 , the oracle permits evaluating $
abla f(u;\omega)$ and $
abla f(u^{\prime};\omega)$ using the same sample $\omega$ . There exists $\ell\geq L$ such that, for every pre-query sigma-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ and every pair of $\mathcal{A}$ -measurable feasible points $u,u^{\prime}\in X	imes Y$ , a fresh sample $\omega\sim\mathcal{D}$ , independent of $\mathcal{A}$ , satisfies $\mathbb{E}\!\left[\lVert
abla f(u;\omega)-
abla f(u^{\prime};\omega)Vert^{2}\,\middle|\,\mathcal{A}ight]\leq\ell^{2}\lVert u-u^{\prime}Vert^{2}.$ (113) Samples within each newly drawn batch are independent, and each batch is independent of the information available before it is drawn. Each sample-gradient evaluation at one point counts as one SFO call; evaluating a paired difference therefore costs two SFO calls.

Theorem 4 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 , 2 , 4 , and 3 hold. Fix a known bound $\overline{B}\geq B$ and set $\begin{gathered}T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{256L\overline{B}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad B_{\rm r}=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{1536C_{\star}\sigma^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}^{2}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\\ A_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}:=\frac{16C_{\star}\chi^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}^{2}},\qquad q=\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{B_{\rm r}}{A_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}}}\right\rfloor\right\},\qquad b=\lceil A_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}q\rceil.\end{gathered}$ (136) Then VR-SPDE returns a point satisfying ( 7 ), and $N_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}\leq B_{\rm r}+18T\min\left\{B_{\rm r},\sqrt{A_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}B_{\rm r}}\right\}.$ (137) For fixed positive $\sigma$ and $\chi$ , the parameter and oracle orders are $\displaystyle T=O(\sqrt{\kappa}\varepsilon^{-2}),\qquad B_{\rm r}=O(\kappa\varepsilon^{-2}),\qquad q=\Theta((\chi\varepsilon)^{-1}),\qquad b=O(\chi\kappa\varepsilon^{-1}),$ (138) $\displaystyle N_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}=O\!\left(\kappa\varepsilon^{-2}+\chi\kappa^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-3}\right).$ If $\sigma=0$ , then $B_{\rm r}=q=1$ and $N_{{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}\leq 3T=O(\sqrt{\kappa}\varepsilon^{-2})$ .

Theorem 5 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 , 2 , and 4 hold. Fix a known bound $\overline{B}\geq B$ independent of $\varepsilon,\tau$ . For $\varepsilon>0$ , choose $\tau$ as in ( 105 ), choose $h,\alpha,k$ by ( 33 ), and choose $\beta$ by ( 79 ). Set $\begin{gathered}T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{512L\overline{B}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad B_{\rm r}=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{3072C_{\star}\sigma^{2}}{\beta^{2}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\\ A_{\rm vr}:=\frac{16C_{\star}\chi^{2}}{\beta^{2}},\qquad q=\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{B_{\rm r}}{A_{\rm vr}}}\right\rfloor\right\},\qquad b=\lceil A_{\rm vr}q\rceil.\end{gathered}$ (139) Then Algorithm 2 satisfies ( 7 ). Its number of stochastic full-gradient oracle calls obeys $\displaystyle N_{\rm vr}$ $\displaystyle\leq B_{\rm r}\left\lceil\frac{3T}{q}\right\rceil+2b\left(3T-\left\lceil\frac{3T}{q}\right\rceil\right)$ $\displaystyle\leq B_{\rm r}+18T\min\{B_{\rm r},\sqrt{A_{\rm vr}B_{\rm r}}\}.$ (140) For fixed problem data, $\overline{B}$ , and $\sigma>0$ , as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ , $T=O(\varepsilon^{-5/2}),\qquad B_{\rm r}=O(\varepsilon^{-3}),\qquad q=\Theta(\varepsilon^{-1}),\qquad b=O(\varepsilon^{-2}),\qquad N_{\rm vr}=O(\varepsilon^{-9/2}).$ (141) If $\sigma=0$ , the choices in ( 139 ) give $B_{\rm r}=q=1$ and $N_{\rm vr}\leq 3T=O(\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ .

Remark 2 . The iteration order remains $O(\varepsilon^{-5/2})$ in both stochastic methods. In SPDE, every iteration pays for three batches of order $\varepsilon^{-5/2}$ . In VR-SPDE, a refresh of order $\varepsilon^{-3}$ is spread over $\Theta(\varepsilon^{-1})$ requests, and the difference batches have order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ . The average oracle work per iteration is therefore $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ for fixed positive variance. The stronger oracle in Assumption 4 enables this improvement. The bounds in Theorems 3 and 5 are upper bounds for the same expected squared game-stationarity criterion.

Theorem 6 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 , 2 , and 3 hold, with the strong-concavity modulus chosen so that $0<\mu\leq L$ ; any larger valid modulus may be replaced by $\min\{\mu,L\}$ . Let $\varepsilon>0$ and fix a known bound $\overline{B}\geq B$ . For SPDE, use the unregularized specialization and the parameters in ( 100 ), and set $T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{16L\overline{B}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad m=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{4800\sigma^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\}.$ (153) Then $\mathbb{E}\mathcal{S}_{\rm OS}(z_{\rm out})^{2}\leq\varepsilon^{2}$ , and the number of SFO calls satisfies $N_{{\rm os},{\rm sc}}\leq 3\left(1+\frac{16L\overline{B}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right)\left(1+\frac{4800\sigma^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right)=O(\kappa\varepsilon^{-4})$ (154) for fixed positive $L,\overline{B}$ , and $\sigma$ . If Assumption 4 also holds, run the unregularized VR-SPDE specialization with $\begin{gathered}T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{32L\overline{B}}{\beta_{\rm sc}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad B_{\rm r}=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{192C_{\star}\sigma^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}^{2}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\\ A_{{\rm os},{\rm sc}}:=\frac{16C_{\star}\chi^{2}}{\beta_{\rm sc}^{2}},\qquad q=\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{B_{\rm r}}{A_{{\rm os},{\rm sc}}}}\right\rfloor\right\},\qquad b=\left\lceil A_{{\rm os},{\rm sc}}q\right\rceil.\end{gathered}$ (155) Then $\mathbb{E}\mathcal{S}_{\rm OS}(z_{\rm out})^{2}\leq\varepsilon^{2}$ and $\displaystyle N_{{\rm os},{\rm vr},{\rm sc}}$ $\displaystyle\leq B_{\rm r}+18T\min\left\{B_{\rm r},\sqrt{A_{{\rm os},{\rm sc}}B_{\rm r}}\right\}$ $\displaystyle=O\!\left(\kappa\varepsilon^{-2}+\chi\kappa^{3/2}\varepsilon^{-3}\right)$ (156) for fixed positive $\sigma$ and $\chi$ . If $\sigma=0$ , both methods use $O(\sqrt{\kappa}\varepsilon^{-2})$ SFO calls.

Theorem 7 . Suppose that Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Let $\varepsilon>0$ , fix a known bound $\overline{B}\geq B$ independent of $\varepsilon$ and $\tau$ , and set $\tau_{\rm os}:=\min\left\{L,\frac{\varepsilon^{2}}{16LD_{Y}^{2}}\right\},\qquad K_{\varepsilon}^{\rm os}:=\max\left\{1,\frac{4LD_{Y}}{\varepsilon}\right\}.$ (157) Choose $h,\alpha,k$ by ( 33 ) and $\beta$ by ( 79 ), with $\tau=\tau_{\rm os}$ . For SPDE, set $T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{64L\overline{B}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad m=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{19200\sigma^{2}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\}.$ (158) Then $\mathbb{E}\mathcal{S}_{\rm OS}(z_{\rm out})^{2}\leq\varepsilon^{2}$ and $\displaystyle N_{{\rm os},{\rm ncc}}$ $\displaystyle\leq 3\left(1+\frac{64L\overline{B}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right)\left(1+\frac{19200\sigma^{2}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right)$ $\displaystyle=O\!\left(1+\frac{(L\overline{B}+\sigma^{2})K_{\varepsilon}^{\rm os}}{\varepsilon^{2}}+\frac{L\overline{B}\sigma^{2}(K_{\varepsilon}^{\rm os})^{2}}{\varepsilon^{4}}\right).$ (159) For fixed problem data, $\overline{B}$ , and $\sigma>0$ , this gives $T=m=O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ and $N_{{\rm os},{\rm ncc}}=O(\varepsilon^{-6})$ . If Assumption 4 also holds, run VR-SPDE with $\begin{gathered}T=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{128L\overline{B}}{\beta\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad B_{\rm r}=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{768C_{\star}\sigma^{2}}{\beta^{2}\varepsilon^{2}}\right\rceil\right\},\\ A_{{\rm os},{\rm ncc}}:=\frac{16C_{\star}\chi^{2}}{\beta^{2}},\qquad q=\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor\sqrt{\frac{B_{\rm r}}{A_{{\rm os},{\rm ncc}}}}\right\rfloor\right\},\qquad b=\left\lceil A_{{\rm os},{\rm ncc}}q\right\rceil.\end{gathered}$ (160) Then $\mathbb{E}\mathcal{S}_{\rm OS}(z_{\rm out})^{2}\leq\varepsilon^{2}$ and $\displaystyle N_{{\rm os},{\rm vr},{\rm ncc}}$ $\displaystyle\leq B_{\rm r}+18T\min\left\{B_{\rm r},\sqrt{A_{{\rm os},{\rm ncc}}B_{\rm r}}\right\}$ $\displaystyle=O(\varepsilon^{-4}+\chi\varepsilon^{-6})=O(\varepsilon^{-6})$ (161) for fixed positive problem data, $\sigma$ , and $\chi$ . If $\sigma=0$ , both methods use $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ SFO calls.
